text.arabic_uthmani: وَأَنكِحُوا۟ ٱلْأَيَٰمَىٰ مِنكُمْ وَٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ مِنْ عِبَادِكُمْ وَإِمَآئِكُمْ ۚ إِن يَكُونُوا۟ فُقَرَآءَ يُغْنِهِمُ ٱللَّهُ مِن فَضْلِهِۦ ۗ وَٱللَّهُ وَٰسِعٌ عَلِيمٌۭ

words.gloss_range: resumptive conjunction opening a continued legal directive
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) opens the ayah as continuation rather than a detached saying. It carries the previous social directive sequence into a new command frame, so marriage facilitation is heard as part of the same public discipline. The connective also begins the ayah's chain of repeated command markers, with the next ayah's restraint command in (24:33) still in view.

topics.headline: opening conjunction carries the legal sequence forward
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the marriage command continues the surrounding social-directive chain rather than starting as isolated advice.
topics.reason: QAC marks the word as a coordinating conjunction, and the clause evidence places the following imperative inside the main directive clause.

topics.headline: command-chain echo is local to the surrounding directives
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the short connector as part of a repeated command architecture stretching across nearby directives, especially into (24:33).
topics.reason: The structural echo survives, while the unsupported reference to a later light-verse transition is narrowed to the local 24:30-33 directive sequence.

words.gloss_range: Form IV plural imperative to cause or facilitate marriage for others
words.root_gloss_range: root range includes marital union and legal marriage bond; local Form IV command selects arranged facilitation rather than self-marriage
words.prose: {{ar:أَنكِحُوا۟}} ({{tr:ankiḥū}}) is a second-person plural imperative, so the addressed community is recruited as the acting facilitator. Its Form IV shape makes the command causative: the addressees are to help others enter marriage, not simply marry themselves. That agency shift is central to the ayah's movement, because the direct objects are the spouseless and the qualified servants, while divine agency later takes over the provision question. The root still belongs to the marriage bond and union field, but local syntax keeps contract-facilitation in front.

topics.headline: plural imperative makes marriage facilitation communal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the command addresses a collective social body, not only the people who need marriage.
topics.reason: QAC identifies a Form IV imperative with second-person masculine plural agreement, and attachment evidence supplies the implicit plural addressee.

topics.headline: Form IV transfers marriage agency outward
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the verb asking the community to cause or arrange marriage for named recipients rather than reading it as self-directed marriage.
topics.reason: The verb governs the recipient groups as objects, and the Form IV tag supports causative facilitation.

topics.headline: marriage-root range is narrowed by the legal command frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader keeps the root's union and contract field in view while seeing that this form selects social arrangement of marriage.
topics.reason: The broader root range is valid background, but local Form IV valency and direct objects narrow the active sense to arranging marriage for others.

topics.headline: command links social structure to provision anxiety
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the marriage command immediately opens toward poverty, provision, and the next ayah's unresolved marriage case (24:33).
topics.reason: The supplied contextual rows tie the command to poverty and provision roots and to the next ayah's marriage vocabulary.

words.gloss_range: the spouseless or unmarried as a definite plural object of the command
words.root_gloss_range: root denotes lack of a spouse across gender and prior marital status; local form makes that state a named legal category
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْأَيَٰمَىٰ}} ({{tr:al-ayāmā}}) is the first direct object of the command, so the spouseless are the group acted for by communal facilitation. The definite plural presents them as a recognized category within the community rather than scattered private cases. Its lexical range is wider than widowhood alone: the spouseless state can include men and women, never-married, divorced, or widowed persons. Because the form is a rare, targeted naming, the ayah gives this social lack unusually explicit legal attention.

topics.headline: definite object makes the spouseless a known target group
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the spouseless as the commanded object's recognized social category, not a side note.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence make the noun definite, plural, accusative, and the direct object of the imperative.

topics.headline: spouselessness is broader than widowhood
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the command covers the spouseless across gender and prior marital history rather than only widows.
topics.reason: The critical lexical rows agree that the noun names people without spouses broadly, and no guardrail narrows it to widowhood.

topics.headline: rare naming gives the category legal weight
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that a rarely named social condition receives direct wording inside the marriage command.
topics.reason: The supplied distribution rows treat the form as uniquely concentrated here, and the local syntax gives that occurrence legal force.

topics.headline: social lack remains active when poverty is tested
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees spouselessness and economic lack brought into relation instead of treated as unrelated issues.
topics.reason: The later plural condition and enrichment suffix resume the command's object list, allowing the spouseless category to remain in view.

words.gloss_range: partitive phrase locating the spouseless within the addressed community

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: prepositional base visible inside the fused phrase

words.prose: {{ar:مِنكُمْ}} ({{tr:minkum}}) attaches the spouseless category to the addressed community. The preposition selects them from among the addressees while the second-person plural suffix makes their need internal to the social body being commanded. It also begins a repeated {{ar:مِن}} ({{tr:min}}) pattern: first internal membership, then servant subset, then divine source.

topics.headline: partitive phrase makes the spouseless internal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the unmarried are from within the addressed community, so the obligation concerns insiders rather than outsiders.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the suffix governed by the preposition as a qualifier of the first object.

topics.headline: first min starts a three-part prepositional sequence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the same particle later shift from human subset selection to divine source marking.
topics.reason: The ayah has three local min-phrases with distinct attachments and functions.

words.gloss_range: coordinating conjunction extending the command's object list
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) adds the qualified servant group under the same marriage-facilitation command. The conjunction does not replace the first object or restart the sentence; it expands the commanded scope from the spouseless among the addressees to the sound or fit among their dependents. That small connector is where the ayah's social range widens.

topics.headline: conjunction extends the same command to another group
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the second group receives the same command rather than becoming a separate or weaker case.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence coordinates the qualified servant group with the first direct object under the one imperative.

topics.headline: social scope widens at the connector
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the ayah move from free community members to servant classes through a single additive hinge.
topics.reason: The conjunction follows the first partitive phrase and introduces the servant-qualified object.

words.gloss_range: the sound, fit, or righteous qualified ones as a conjoined object drawn from the servant classes
words.root_gloss_range: root range includes soundness against corruption, fitness, repair, and reconciliation; local active participle selects stable moral and functional suitability
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ}} ({{tr:al-ṣāliḥīna}}) is accusative as the second object under the marriage command, while the following partitive phrase identifies the servant classes from whom they are drawn. The definite active participle makes eligibility a recognized quality: soundness, fitness, and freedom from corruption are the criterion, not free status or wealth. The repair and rightness field gives the phrase positive social force, but local grammar keeps it as a qualification of servant candidates rather than a general virtue slogan.

topics.headline: accusative participle marks the eligible servant subset
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees servant candidates included through a named eligibility filter rather than by status alone.
topics.reason: The word is an accusative conjoined object, and the following min-phrase specifies the servant source class.

topics.headline: soundness and fitness become the local marriage criterion
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that eligibility is framed by moral and functional soundness rather than by wealth or freedom.
topics.reason: V4 supports soundness against corruption and suitability branches, while local syntax narrows the branch to qualifying servant marriage candidates.

topics.headline: active participle presents settled suitability
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the qualification as an enduring recognized condition that can govern both male and female servant classes.
topics.reason: QAC tags the word as an active participle, and the paired servant nouns follow under the same qualification.

topics.headline: soundness carries the prior moral sequence into eligibility
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the marriage command inherit the surrounding concern with moral repair and ordered social relations.
topics.reason: The contextual rows connect the root to servant status, divine promise, and the surrounding moral sequence.

words.gloss_range: partitive preposition drawing the qualified ones from servant classes

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: earlier partitive phrase selecting the spouseless from within the addressed community

words.prose: {{ar:مِنْ}} ({{tr:min}}) makes the qualified ones a subset from the servant classes named next. It prevents the phrase from flattening all servants into an automatic marriage category: the selected group is the sound or fit among them. In the ayah's repeated prepositional architecture, this second {{ar:مِنْ}} ({{tr:min}}) parallels {{ar:مِنكُمْ}} ({{tr:minkum}}) but shifts to a different social register.

topics.headline: partitive min selects from servants
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the command includes the qualified among servants, not an unfiltered category detached from the eligibility term.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the preposition govern the servant noun as complement to the qualified participle.

topics.headline: parallel min phrases mark two social scopes
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees identical prepositional architecture distinguish free community members from servant dependents.
topics.reason: The first two min-phrases both mark human subsets but attach to different recipient groups.

words.gloss_range: your male servants or bonded dependents, genitive under the partitive phrase
words.root_gloss_range: root range includes owned servitude, creaturely servanthood to God, worshipful service, subjugation, and smoothing; local noun selects human servant status with dignity-pressure from the chosen plural

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: preceding partitive preposition governing the servant noun
reported variant with a more chattel-marked servant plural

words.prose: {{ar:عِبَادِكُمْ}} ({{tr:ʿibādikum}}) is governed by the preceding {{ar:مِنْ}} ({{tr:min}}), so servant status is subordinate to the eligibility term rather than standing as a separate object. The possessive suffix names the community's social control and responsibility at once: these are your dependents, and the command acts on that relationship. The chosen plural carries a dignifying pressure, especially beside the reported {{ar:عَبِيدِكُمْ}} ({{tr:ʿabīdikum}}) variant, while the local phrase still refers to human servants rather than replacing social servitude with a purely devotional meaning. The road-smoothing branch adds a smaller image of making a passable route into marriage, kept as background pressure by the local noun phrase.

topics.headline: genitive servant noun remains under the qualifier
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees servant status grammatically subordinated to the qualified eligibility phrase rather than made an independent object.
topics.reason: QAC marks the noun genitive, and attachment evidence makes it the complement of the partitive preposition.

topics.headline: possessive suffix exposes control and obligation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the same possessive relation naming dependence becomes the ground for communal responsibility.
topics.reason: The second-person plural suffix is part of the governed noun and binds the servant class to the addressed community.

topics.headline: standard plural dignifies without erasing servitude
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the standard plural's dignity-pressure against a more chattel-marked variant while keeping the local servant status intact.
topics.reason: V4 includes both owned servitude and creaturely servanthood branches; local possessive and prepositional syntax select human servants, while the variant contrast preserves register pressure.

topics.headline: servitude root opens dignity and pathway associations
topics.reader_payoff: The reader can hear servant inclusion against broader servanthood and passable-route imagery, without letting those branches control the local parse.
topics.reason: The broader root branches are real but not locally selected as the main sense; they survive as lexical pressure around servant inclusion.

words.gloss_range: coordinating conjunction joining female servants under the same partitive phrase

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: preceding partitive preposition governing both servant nouns

words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) joins the female servants to the male servants under the same preceding {{ar:مِنْ}} ({{tr:min}}). The conjunction does not restart the phrase; it completes the servant pair inside one governed construction. Its payoff is explicit inclusion: female servants are named rather than left to be inferred under masculine servant language.

topics.headline: conjunction keeps both servant groups under one min
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees male and female servants governed by the same partitive phrase and eligibility frame.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence joins the female servant noun to the male servant noun under the earlier preposition.

topics.headline: connector makes the female servant class explicit
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that female servants are not silently absorbed into a masculine plural but explicitly added.
topics.reason: The conjunction immediately precedes the distinct female-servant noun and completes the servant pair.

words.gloss_range: your female servants, genitive and coordinated with the male servant noun
words.root_gloss_range: local root evidence is concentrated in this feminine servant noun; the active sense is sex-specific female servant inclusion

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: preceding partitive preposition shared by the coordinated servant nouns

words.prose: {{ar:إِمَآئِكُمْ}} ({{tr:imāʾikum}}) shares the governance of the preceding {{ar:مِنْ}} ({{tr:min}}) with the male servant noun. Its possessive suffix mirrors the same social responsibility toward female dependents. The feminine broken plural makes female servant inclusion formal and visible, not an afterthought, and its rare distribution concentrates that legal inclusion in this verse.

topics.headline: female servant noun shares the same governed phrase
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees female servants placed under the same eligibility and communal-responsibility frame as male servants.
topics.reason: QAC marks the noun genitive with a possessive suffix, and attachment evidence coordinates it with the prior servant noun.

topics.headline: feminine plural names female servants directly
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that female servants are named in their own formal plural instead of being implied under male-servant wording.
topics.reason: The noun is a feminine servant counterpart and is coordinated explicitly after the male servant class.

topics.headline: hapax concentration sharpens the inclusion
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that a uniquely concentrated term is used exactly where female servant inclusion must not be missed.
topics.reason: The supplied distribution rows identify the form/root as uniquely occurring here, and local syntax gives it legal function.

topics.headline: servant pair is closed by sex-specific naming
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the servant class distributed by male and female naming after one moral qualification.
topics.reason: The local pair is formed by the male servant noun plus this female servant noun under the same construction.

words.gloss_range: conditional particle introducing a possible poverty condition and its divine answer
words.prose: {{ar:إِنْ}} ({{tr:in}}) opens the poverty clause as a condition, not as a fixed description of the listed groups. It governs the dependent verb and structures the enrichment clause as the answer, turning a possible objection into a promise frame. Because it comes after the full recipient list, poverty is tested across all named marriage candidates rather than attached to only one class.

topics.headline: conditional particle governs objection and answer
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees poverty and divine enrichment bound into one conditional-promise structure.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence separates protasis and apodosis and links them under the condition.

topics.headline: poverty is possible, not assumed identity
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah does not mark the unmarried or servants as inherently poor; need is a condition if present.
topics.reason: The conditional particle frames the following poverty predicate as hypothetical and dependent.

topics.headline: condition begins after all recipients are named
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the poverty test apply to the entire recipient list rather than only the last named group.
topics.reason: The condition starts after the main command's object list is complete, and later pronoun evidence resumes that list.

words.gloss_range: jussive copular verb hosting poverty as a possible state of the listed recipients
words.root_gloss_range: root range centers on being, becoming, and state; local Form I copula hosts a predicate without making poverty an essence

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: following enrichment verb that reverses poverty
conditional particle controlling the dependent poverty clause

words.prose: {{ar:يَكُونُوا۟}} ({{tr:yakūnū}}) carries a hidden plural subject back to the marriage candidates already named. Its jussive form is controlled by {{ar:إِنْ}} ({{tr:in}}), so the poverty clause remains hypothetical. As a simple copula, it hosts poverty as a state they may be in, not as an identity formed into them; this prepares the reversal by {{ar:يُغْنِهِمُ}} ({{tr:yughnihimu}}).

topics.headline: hidden plural subject gathers the listed recipients
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the condition refer back to the named marriage candidates rather than an unspecified third party.
topics.reason: The finite verb carries third-person masculine plural agreement, and attachment evidence notes an implicit subject with the earlier recipient span as the natural referent.

topics.headline: jussive form keeps the poverty clause dependent
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the poverty statement is grammatically subordinate to the conditional frame.
topics.reason: QAC marks the verb as jussive under the conditional particle, and clause evidence places it in the protasis.

topics.headline: copula hosts poverty as state, not essence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees poverty as a condition that can be answered, not a permanent identity assigned to the recipients.
topics.reason: The copular verb takes poverty as predicate, and local grammar avoids stronger formation or transformation claims.

topics.headline: being-state sets up divine change
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees a possible state of lack staged for a following act of enrichment.
topics.reason: The local protasis-apodosis sequence moves from the copular poverty state to the enrichment verb.

words.gloss_range: poor or lacking as an accusative predicate state in the conditional clause
words.root_gloss_range: root range includes poverty, need, fracture, hollowing, and lack; local predicate selects economic insufficiency that divine sufficiency can reverse

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: following enrichment verb that reverses poverty

words.prose: {{ar:فُقَرَآءَ}} ({{tr:fuqarāʾa}}) is the predicate of the copula, so poverty is grammatically a condition they may occupy rather than a permanent label. Its root field gives economic need the feel of fracture or hollowing, a depletion that the next verb answers. The local contrast with {{ar:يُغْنِهِمُ}} ({{tr:yughnihimu}}) turns the condition into an antonymic movement from lack to sufficiency, while the faqīr distinction keeps the claim short of total destitution.

topics.headline: accusative predicate makes poverty detachable
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that poverty is framed as a state within the condition, not a fixed identity for the recipients.
topics.reason: QAC marks the adjective accusative, and attachment evidence identifies it as the predicate of the copular verb.

topics.headline: poverty is staged for reversal by sufficiency
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the ayah build a root-level economic reversal from lack to sufficiency.
topics.reason: The following apodosis uses the enrichment root, and the supplied cooccurrence rows identify this as a marked antonym field.

topics.headline: fracture and hollowing imagery color economic need
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels poverty as structural depletion that can be filled or repaired, while local grammar keeps economic need as the selected sense.
topics.reason: The root imagery supports fracture and hollowing, but the local adjective in a poverty condition selects socioeconomic insufficiency.

topics.headline: faqir need is not flattened into absolute destitution
topics.reader_payoff: The reader recognizes a meaningful need condition without overreading it as total absence of every resource.
topics.reason: The lexical distinction preserves insufficiency as the local sense, while boundary and synthesis rows connect that need to divine repair.

words.gloss_range: Form IV jussive apodosis meaning He will make them sufficient or enrich them
words.root_gloss_range: root range includes freedom from need, sufficiency, wealth, and richness; local Form IV selects causing the recipients to become sufficient
words.prose: {{ar:يُغْنِهِمُ}} ({{tr:yughnihimu}}) is the apodosis of the condition: if poverty is present, the answer is divine causing-to-suffice. The attached object suffix gathers the whole recipient list compactly, so the promise covers the spouseless and qualified servants together. The root reverses poverty as freedom from need, not merely accumulation of wealth, and the Form IV shape makes the change active. The phrase also belongs to a provision formula echoed in (9:28) and taken up again in (24:33).

topics.headline: jussive enrichment answers the poverty condition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees enrichment as the grammatical answer to possible poverty, not an unrelated assurance.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence identifies the verb as the apodosis linked to the poverty protasis.

topics.headline: object suffix compacts all recipients
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the promise resumes the full marriage-candidate list in one suffix.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the suffix the object of the verb and links it to the earlier recipient span.

topics.headline: Form IV causes sufficiency, not mere wealth display
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the promised change as being made free from need rather than simply receiving surplus possessions.
topics.reason: The root supports sufficiency and wealth, while local Form IV and poverty contrast narrow the payoff to causing sufficiency in the recipients.

topics.headline: enrichment formula links this promise to other provision scenes
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that this marriage-poverty answer uses a recognizable divine-provision formula also echoed in (9:28) and (24:33).
topics.reason: The supplied rows cite the formula in (9:28) and the immediate next-ayah reuse in (24:33).

words.gloss_range: divine proper name as explicit subject of the enrichment verb
words.root_gloss_range: divine-name field includes worship, deity, refuge, and contested derivational associations; local function is the named divine subject who enriches
words.prose: {{ar:ٱللَّهُ}} ({{tr:Allāhu}}) is the explicit subject of the enrichment verb. The community facilitates marriage, but the provision answer is assigned to God, so social agency and divine agency are separated rather than confused. Naming the subject rather than leaving it implicit anchors the economic promise in the divine name, and its placement between the verb and source phrase routes the movement from need through divine agency to divine bounty.

topics.headline: divine name is the subject of enrichment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that actual enrichment is grammatically assigned to God rather than to communal action.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence identifies the proper noun as the explicit subject of the enrichment verb.

topics.headline: agency shifts from community to divine provider
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the ayah divide responsibility: humans facilitate marriage, while God answers the provision anxiety.
topics.reason: The imperative's implicit plural subject differs from the explicit divine subject in the apodosis.

topics.headline: divine-name derivation colors the provider without controlling syntax
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the provider as the named deity of worship and turning, while the local grammar remains the subject relation.
topics.reason: The derivational dispute is useful background for the divine name, but the local payoff is its explicit subject role.

topics.headline: first divine subject anticipates the attribute subject
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the first divine subject performing enrichment and the later divine subject grounding it with attributes, with the formula repeated in (24:33).
topics.reason: The ayah repeats the divine name as verbal subject and nominal subject, and the supplied row cites the phrase's reuse in (24:33).

words.gloss_range: source preposition marking divine bounty as the origin of enrichment

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: following possessive bounty phrase governed as the source of enrichment

words.prose: {{ar:مِن}} ({{tr:min}}) is the third min-phrase, but its function has changed. The first two min-phrases select human subsets; this one marks the source from which enrichment proceeds. By governing {{ar:فَضْلِهِۦ}} ({{tr:faḍlihī}}), the particle turns divine bounty into the channel or reservoir of sufficiency.

topics.headline: third min marks source rather than subset
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that provision is sourced from divine bounty, not merely governed by another partitive phrase.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the bounty noun the complement of the preposition after the enrichment verb.

topics.headline: same particle shifts from selection to provision
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees one repeated particle carry the ayah from human classification into divine sourcing.
topics.reason: The ayah contains two earlier human subset min-phrases and this later source min-phrase.

words.gloss_range: His bounty, favor, or surplus as the genitive source of enrichment
words.root_gloss_range: root range includes surplus, excess, favor, preference, and bestowal; local possessive source phrase selects God's own bounty as provision reservoir

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: preceding source preposition governing the bounty phrase

words.prose: {{ar:فَضْلِهِۦ}} ({{tr:faḍlihī}}) is governed by source {{ar:مِن}} ({{tr:min}}), so divine bounty is grammatically the origin of enrichment. The possessive suffix binds the source to God rather than to communal wealth. The root's surplus and favor field makes the promise feel like provision from overflow, not competition for a finite human pool, and the phrase participates in a provision formula also visible in (4:32) and (9:28). Within Surah 24, the same root also connects divine and human surplus in (24:22) and (24:10).

topics.headline: possessive bounty is the source of enrichment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that enrichment comes from God's own bounty, not from an impersonal resource or communal purse.
topics.reason: QAC marks the noun genitive with a possessive suffix, and attachment evidence governs it under source min after the enrichment verb.

topics.headline: faḍl names overflow and favor as provision source
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the provision coming from surplus and favor rather than a finite pool that the poor must compete for.
topics.reason: The broader root range supports excess and favor, while local syntax narrows it to God's bounty as the source of enrichment.

topics.headline: verbal noun lets bounty function as reservoir
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees bounty grammatically shaped as a source from which sufficiency can proceed and then warranted by capacity.
topics.reason: QAC tags the word as a verbal noun, and the source preposition governs it as the enrichment source.

topics.headline: faḍl phrase joins wider provision and Surah 24 threads
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the bounty phrase is both a broader provision formula and a Surah 24 thread joining pardon, generosity, and marriage provision.
topics.reason: The supplied rows cite formula parallels in (4:32) and (9:28), plus Surah-local links in (24:10) and (24:22).

words.gloss_range: resumptive conjunction opening the independent attribute coda
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) opens a new nominal coda after the conditional promise. It is not merely another object-list connector; it resumes into an independent attribute statement that explains why the promise can be trusted. The ayah's conjunctions therefore frame the whole movement: opening directive, internal expansion, and closing theological warrant.

topics.headline: resumptive wa opens an attribute coda
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a shift from promised action to the attributes that ground that promise.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence treats words 18-21 as an independent nominal clause.

topics.headline: closing wa turns promise into attribute seal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the ayah's legal command close with a theological warrant rather than ending at the provision event.
topics.reason: The final conjunction introduces the nominal attribute clause after the conditional apodosis.

words.gloss_range: divine proper name as subject of the nominal attribute coda
words.root_gloss_range: divine-name field includes worship, deity, refuge, and contested derivational associations; local function is the explicit nominal subject of the double predicate
words.prose: {{ar:ٱللَّهُ}} ({{tr:Allāhu}}) begins the nominal coda whose predicates are breadth and knowledge. Repeating the divine name instead of using a pronoun fixes the attribute seal on the same one who enriches. The first occurrence performs the provision act; this second occurrence states the standing attributes that warrant it.

topics.headline: divine name begins the double-predicate coda
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the closing attributes predicated directly of God as the coda's subject.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the final words an independent nominal clause with two predicates of the divine subject.

topics.headline: repeated divine name ties action to warrant
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the actor who enriches is explicitly repeated as the subject whose attributes explain the action.
topics.reason: The divine name appears first as the subject of the verb and then as the subject of the nominal coda.

topics.headline: coda generalizes the poverty promise
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the specific marriage-poverty promise grounded in a general truth about divine capacity and knowledge.
topics.reason: The independent nominal clause follows the conditional promise and states stable predicates.

topics.headline: divine-name derivation colors the coda subject

words.gloss_range: vast, capacious, or ample as the first predicate of the divine coda
words.root_gloss_range: root range includes spatial breadth, ample means, capacity, and wideness; local active participle predicates stable divine capacity for provision

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: following knowledge predicate paired with capacity in the coda

words.prose: {{ar:وَٰسِعٌ}} ({{tr:wāsiʿun}}) is the first predicate of the coda, so capacity is stated before knowledge is added. The root's breadth field becomes provision language here: after poverty and bounty, God is vast enough for the named need. Its active participle and indefinite predicate form present capaciousness as a standing, unbounded quality, and the pairing with {{ar:عَلِيمٌ}} ({{tr:ʿalīmun}}) works as a two-part warranty signaled in (2:247) and (2:268), with human capacity mirrored by divine breadth in (2:286).

topics.headline: first coda predicate answers capacity anxiety
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the poverty concern answered first by divine capacity: the source is wide enough for the need.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes this word a predicate of the divine subject in the nominal coda.

topics.headline: spatial breadth becomes provision capacity
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels abstract provision as widened room and ample resource-space, while local context keeps it tied to sufficiency.
topics.reason: The root supports physical breadth and capacity, and the local context after enrichment narrows that image to provision.

topics.headline: participle and indefiniteness make capacity standing and open-ended
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that vastness is presented as a stable qualitative predicate, not a bounded title.
topics.reason: QAC tags the word as an active participle predicate, and the surface carries indefinite predicate cadence.

topics.headline: capacity pairs with knowledge as provision warranty
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the coda's first attribute as one half of a provision formula: capacity plus targeting knowledge, with parallels in (2:247) and (2:268) and a human-capacity mirror in (2:286).
topics.reason: The supplied rows cite the recurring pairing and distinguish capacity from the knowledge predicate that follows.

words.gloss_range: knowing, all-knowing, or intensely knowledgeable as the second predicate of the divine coda
words.root_gloss_range: root range includes knowing, recognizing, teaching, informing, and marking; local faʿīl predicate selects complete stable knowledge applied to provision

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: preceding capacity predicate paired with knowledge in the coda

words.prose: {{ar:عَلِيمٌ}} ({{tr:ʿalīmun}}) completes the coda as the second predicate. After {{ar:وَٰسِعٌ}} ({{tr:wāsiʿun}}) answers whether provision has capacity, this word answers whether provision is known, measured, and suited to actual recipients. The intensive faʿīl pattern makes the knowledge stable and complete, and the final position gives closure-weight to precision, not abundance alone. In Surah 24's dense knowledge thread, the closing seal applies divine knowledge to hidden social and economic circumstances.

topics.headline: second predicate binds knowledge to capacity
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the coda as a compound warranty: God has both capacity and knowledge for the provision promise.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes this word a second predicate of the same divine subject.

topics.headline: faʿīl pattern intensifies stable knowledge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears more than bare awareness: the promise is backed by enduring, complete knowledge.
topics.reason: The form supports intensive knowledge, while local predication ties that force to the provision coda.

topics.headline: knowledge gives precision to the promise
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that divine provision is not blind abundance; it is suited to who needs what.
topics.reason: The predicate follows capacity in the paired coda, and the supplied rows define the pair as capacity plus targeting precision.

topics.headline: final knowledge word seals the ayah
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the ayah close on knowledge, so the social command is ringed by divine capacity and precision.
topics.reason: The word is final in the ayah and completes the paired predicate cadence.

topics.headline: Surah 24 knowledge thread specializes the seal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees a familiar divine-knowledge seal specialized to marriage, poverty, and social vulnerability.
topics.reason: The supplied rows connect the root with divine-name cooccurrence and Surah 24's knowledge pattern.

topics.headline: indefinite predicate mirrors the first coda attribute
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees knowledge paired formally with capacity as a qualitative predicate rather than a separate title.
topics.reason: The final predicate parallels the preceding indefinite predicate under the same divine subject.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The plural causative imperative at 24:32:1 and its objects, the unpartnered and suitable dependents.
baseline_models.mechanism: The causative marriage branch assigns the addressees an enabling role: they are to bring other people into a marriage bond, so lack of a spouse is treated as a communal coordination problem as well as an individual condition.

activation_trace.role: Causing another to marry is the literal branch and makes communal facilitation the operative mechanism.

changed_reading.before: A general endorsement of individuals marrying.
changed_reading.after: A plural charge to those with social agency to cause marriages to become possible for others.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The coordinated groups at 24:32:2-7, especially the suitable among male and female slaves.
baseline_models.mechanism: Suitability, not freedom or existing wealth, is the stated positive filter. The command crosses the free-servile boundary and includes owned men and women within the community's marriage-enabling responsibility.

activation_trace.role: Fitness and compatibility are the literal branch and supply the eligibility criterion.
Owned servitude is the literal status named and marks a boundary the command crosses.
The owned woman is the literal branch and makes female slaves explicit beneficiaries rather than an implied remainder.
Causing marriage supplies the common action applied across the listed statuses.

changed_reading.before: Marriage support is primarily for already independent and economically established people.
changed_reading.after: Practical suitability can ground marriage support across status, including for owned dependents.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The conditional sequence at 24:32:9-17: if they are poor, God will suffice them from His surplus, and God is expansive and knowing.
baseline_models.mechanism: Present need is not made a veto. Sufficiency is grammatically placed after the marriage command and is sourced in gift and expansive capacity, while knowledge keeps the promise attentive to actual conditions.

activation_trace.role: Material need and small means are the literal branch and name the apparent barrier.
Making another sufficient is the literal branch and supplies the promised reversal of need.
Gracious gift beyond obligation is the literal source from which sufficiency comes.
Amplitude of wealth and livelihood is the literal branch and removes a zero-sum ceiling from the promise.
Knowledge as disclosed awareness qualifies expansiveness as informed rather than indiscriminate.

changed_reading.before: Economic surplus must exist before marriage can responsibly begin.
changed_reading.after: Need does not itself disqualify: sufficiency may arise after entry into the supported bond.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The close sequence of marry, poor, enrich, and surplus at 24:32.
baseline_models.mechanism: The enrichment inventory itself includes marriage as a form of fortifying the unmarried. That permits a non-pecuniary baseline in which the bond can produce a kind of sufficiency even before any increase in cash.

activation_trace.role: Enrichment through marriage is the literal branch and lets the promise include relational fortification.
The marriage contract is the literal bond that could instantiate this non-pecuniary sufficiency.
Gift beyond obligation keeps the resulting sufficiency broader than earned wages alone.

changed_reading.before: God will enrich them means only that their monetary holdings will increase.
changed_reading.after: The marriage bond itself may be one component of the sufficiency and fortification promised.

context_deltas.mechanism: Whole-surah repetitions turn divine provision into a circulation system. People who possess surplus and means are told to give; emancipating dependents are given from wealth called God's; provision is apportioned; and kin households share edible portions. God's sufficing can therefore arrive through commanded human transfers without ceasing to be God's gift.

activation_trace.role: Concrete need is the focus deficit that the circulation must answer.
Making others sufficient is the focus outcome re-read as potentially mediated.
Surplus and remainder are literal resources held by people and made available for distribution.
Human amplitude of wealth and livelihood identifies agents able to carry provision.
Giving is the literal action that converts possessed amplitude into another's support.
The repeated giving root marks both God's prior grant and the required onward transfer to dependents.
Possessed wealth is the material routed from divine source to a person seeking release.
Apportioned gift names divine provision while leaving its delivery channel open.
An edible share is the literal branch and extends provision into the kin-household network.

structural_cues: 24:22 couples possessors of surplus and means with an imperative to give to vulnerable relations and migrants.
24:33 calls the transferred funds God's wealth that God first gave the current holders.
24:61 permits eating across a wide kin-house network, together or separately.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies repeated surplus, capacity, giving, divine wealth, apportioned provision, and shared food; I infer the arrow from divine source through human redistribution to the poor couple. A direct or otherwise unseen act of provision remains a live alternative.

changed_reading.before: The poverty clause predicts a private windfall delivered independently of the community.
changed_reading.after: Divine sufficiency can be realized through the community's commanded circulation of surplus, grants, and household provision.

context_deltas.mechanism: The next ayah acknowledges people who cannot obtain marriage and gives them a chastity-until-sufficiency path; the later ayah recognizes women who no longer expect marriage and again values chastity. The focus imperative therefore mobilizes facilitators without making immediate marriage compulsory for every unpartnered person.

activation_trace.role: Causing others to marry places the focus obligation on enabling addressees.
Finding or obtaining is the literal branch, and its negation acknowledges real unavailability.
The marriage bond is the unavailable object rather than an act demanded regardless of conditions.
Refraining from what is improper supplies an affirmative conduct for the waiting interval.
Arrival at independence or freedom from need marks the temporal endpoint of waiting.
Women who have ceased expecting menstruation or marriage are a literal recognized category outside an immediate-marriage trajectory.
Hope as orientation to an expected outcome makes non-expectation of marriage explicit.
The same marriage bond is here something not anticipated, limiting a universalizing reading of the focus.
Chosen restraint is again valued and preserves a non-marriage path within the surah.

structural_cues: 24:32 addresses those who can arrange marriage; 24:33 immediately addresses those who cannot obtain it.
The word until in 24:33 makes waiting conditional and temporal rather than a failure.
24:60 explicitly recognizes a class not expecting marriage and describes restraint as better for them.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies distinct addressees, inability, an interval of restraint, and later non-expectation; I infer that the plural command is facilitative rather than coercive. A narrower reading that treats 24:60 as an unrelated age-specific exception remains possible.

changed_reading.before: Every unpartnered person is under pressure to marry immediately, with poverty dismissed as irrelevant.
changed_reading.after: The community must open viable paths to marriage, while candidates retain a recognized waiting or non-marriage path when the bond is unavailable or not expected.

context_deltas.mechanism: The run from house-entry permission through guarded sexual boundaries, named husbands, marriage, and fortification frames the bond as an authorized household threshold. Marriage does not simply permit sex; it creates a protected relation whose access remains structured by enclosure, permission, and restraint.

activation_trace.role: The marriage contract is the focus anchor that can create an authorized relational boundary.
The marriage-house branch lets the surrounding houses function as a model of bounded domestic relation.
Permission and authorization are the literal threshold rule for entering protected space.
Guarding sexual inviolability is the literal branch and defines what the institution must preserve.
The private opening is the literal object guarded before the marriage command.
Husbands are the explicitly named spouse relation within the controlled disclosure network.
Fortification by contract or inviolability gives the bond its protective rather than merely permissive function.

structural_cues: 24:27-29 regulate entry into houses by recognition and permission.
24:30-31 symmetrically command guarding of private parts before naming husbands among bounded relations.
24:33 opposes coerced sexual commerce to a woman's desire for fortification.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies domestic thresholds, permission, guarded sexuality, spouses, and fortification; I infer that marriage joins these into protected household access. The norms could instead be read as neighboring but institutionally independent commands.

changed_reading.before: Marriage is chiefly a status change or a license for sexual access.
changed_reading.after: Marriage is an authorized household enclosure that makes intimacy legitimate by preserving boundaries rather than erasing them.

context_deltas.mechanism: The slave-inclusive focus is immediately followed by funded manumission contracts and a ban on forcing owned young women into sexual commerce when they seek fortification. Later, servitude is directed exclusively toward God within a promised change from fear to security. Marriage support thus sits inside a wider program that limits owners' extraction and opens owned people toward covenant, resources, and agency.

activation_trace.role: Owned servitude is the literal focus status whose treatment is being changed.
The owned woman is explicitly included in the marriage-enabling command.
A slave's written contract for release is the literal branch and supplies a status-exit mechanism.
Required giving funds the dependent rather than merely releasing the owner's claim.
Forcing another into what she rejects is the literal mechanism explicitly prohibited.
The euphemism for an owned young woman identifies the person protected from the owner's extraction.
Sexual commerce is the exploitative branch contrasted with her sought fortification.
Guarded sexual integrity is the woman's stated aim and makes her agency visible.
Submissive worship is redirected to God and supplies the later horizon beyond human ownership.
Changing one condition into another supports a surah-level movement from fear and subjection toward security.

structural_cues: 24:33 immediately follows the marriage command with contract, assessment, funding, anti-coercion, and fortification clauses.
The same verse distinguishes what the dependents seek from what owners may seek to extract.
24:55 pairs social establishment and changed security with worship of God alone.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies adjacent legal-economic protections and a later exclusive-worship horizon; I infer a common arrow from owned object toward protected agent. The marriage, manumission, and anti-prostitution rules may also be independent remedies rather than one staged program.

changed_reading.before: Male and female slaves are passive beneficiaries whom owners simply place into marriages.
changed_reading.after: Their inclusion is part of an anti-exploitative framework that recognizes desire, funds possible release, blocks sexual coercion, and makes marriage one protected covenantal option.

context_deltas.mechanism: Across the surah, the suitability root appears as repair after wrongdoing and as performed good works, while human sponsors are asked to discern beneficial capacity in dependents before contracting release. This shifts the focus adjective from a fixed prestige label toward repairable, enacted, and assessable fitness.

activation_trace.role: Fitness and compatibility are the focus branch whose temporality is being revised.
Repair as the opposite of corruption makes soundness something people can actively restore.
Knowing as disclosed recognition makes human assessment part of enabling a dependent's transition.
Beneficial good is the capacity to be discerned rather than a hereditary status.
Soundness appears as performed works, reinforcing an enacted rather than merely ascribed quality.
Enablement and established capacity show good action issuing into viable social standing.
Security and trust are the condition into which the community is moved, not a status presumed in advance.

structural_cues: 24:5 places repair after a prior offense.
24:33 requires sponsors to know good in dependents before supporting a contract.
24:55 links good works with establishment and a change from fear to security.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies repair, performed good, discerned benefit, and enablement; I infer that suitability can develop and be socially recognized. The focus adjective may still mean a simpler fixed predicate such as morally righteous.

changed_reading.before: The suitable are a prequalified moral class already complete before support begins.
changed_reading.after: Suitability can include practical fit and demonstrated capacity that is repaired, enacted, discerned, and enabled.

context_deltas.mechanism: The next ayah repeats marriage, God's enriching, and surplus, then opposes sexual coercion to sought fortification. Together with the enrichment branch that explicitly overlaps marriage, this strengthens a coexisting reading in which the bond itself supplies protected relational sufficiency, not only later income.

activation_trace.role: Marriage as enrichment is the focus branch whose contextual recurrence is being tested.
The marriage contract supplies the relation capable of functioning as fortification.
Immediate repetition keeps the formal marriage bond beside the repeated enrichment promise.
The same marriage-enrichment branch permits sufficiency here to remain partly relational.
Restraint names the vulnerable interval that a protected bond can help resolve.
Fortification by contract or inviolability supplies the protective effect of relational sufficiency.
Gracious gift keeps both material and relational forms of sufficiency under the same source.

structural_cues: 24:33 immediately repeats the focus sequence marriage, enrichment, God, and surplus.
The latter half of 24:33 makes sought fortification the opposite of coerced sexual exploitation.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies lexical overlap between enrichment and marriage plus the adjacent fortification contrast; I infer that the bond can be part of what enriches. A strictly pecuniary sense of the verb remains materially live.

changed_reading.before: The promise concerns only money acquired after marriage.
changed_reading.after: The protected relation itself may be one gift of sufficiency, alongside any later material increase.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it transfers a cloud mechanism into social provision. It remains packet-anchored through poverty's hollow branch, causative marriage, and 24:43's joining, accumulation, gap, and rain sequence; downstream prose should label it an exploratory material analogy, not a lexical gloss or guaranteed causal law.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The poverty term at 24:32:10 and the causative marriage command at 24:32:1.

activation_trace.role: A hollow or outlet in the ground lets need be imaged as a gap rather than only a quantity of missing cash.
Causing a bond supplies the social act of bringing separated units into relation.
Joining one thing to another supplies the first material operation in the analogy.
Accumulation into a mass shows joined units gaining productive capacity.
A need that fills a gap links the rain passage back to the focus image of lack.
Descending rain is the material yield that emerges after joining and accumulation.

changed_reading.before: Poverty is a sealed absence that must be filled before any bond is formed.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, visible need can be the gap around which coordinated joining accumulates a provision-bearing structure, as joined clouds yield rain through their interstices.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is form-distant because it uses the packet's non-dominant mapping of the focus root as an anti-reading, not as the surface word's direct sense. It remains valid as a contained warning anchored in the plural imperative and 24:22's giving by people of means; downstream prose should say that wideness must not be confused with social abandonment, not that the adjective literally means neglect.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The closing divine attribute at 24:32:16 read beside the opening plural imperative.

activation_trace.role: Spatial or practical expansiveness is the dominant literal branch of the divine attribute.
The split-root image of letting livestock wander into loss supplies the deliberately contained anti-reading.
The plural duty to cause marriages prevents divine amplitude from erasing human responsibility.
Human means and ample livelihood identify capacity that must remain socially active.
The command to give turns amplitude into care rather than laissez-faire release.

changed_reading.before: Because God is vast, the community may leave poor unpartnered people entirely to divine provision.
changed_reading.after: As a split-root anti-reading, divine wideness cannot be invoked to let vulnerable people drift; the community's own amplitude must move toward active facilitation.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates the packet's split mapping from the owned-woman token toward mother and household center; it does not claim that the token literally means mother. It remains anchored by the paired mapped inventories, 24:33's anti-coercion, and 24:61's mothers within the house network; downstream prose should present it as a counter-status resonance that restores latent kin-generating personhood.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The explicitly named female slaves at 24:32:7 within a command to establish marriage.

activation_trace.role: The owned woman is the literal status from which the counter-status activation begins.
The split mapped image of mother as bearer and nurturer exposes a possible kin-generating future not exhausted by ownership.
The euphemism for an owned young woman keeps the same vulnerable person in view after the marriage command.
The ban on forcing her protects the agency needed for any genuine transition into kinship.
Mothers as literal nurturers appear inside the later kin-household resource network.
Household members and dependents form the network into which the counter-status reading imagines incorporation.

changed_reading.before: The female slave is a property subclass whom an owner may assign a spouse.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, the command recognizes an owned woman as a possible origin and nurturer of kin whose personhood cannot be contained by her current property status.

strongest_changes: God's enriching can be mediated through commanded circulation of surplus, grants, and household provision.
The plural marriage command is facilitative rather than coercive because the surah preserves waiting and non-marriage paths.
Marriage becomes a protected household threshold, not an erasure of privacy or sexual boundaries.
The slave-inclusive clause is re-situated among funded release, anti-coercion, and sought fortification.
Enrichment can coexistently include relational sufficiency, not only money.
summary.what_was_special: The whole-surah packet linked the focus cluster to repeated surplus and means, explicit onward giving, household food access, anti-exploitation rules, social establishment, and a material joining-to-rain sequence; the split mappings for wideness and the owned-woman term also generated contained counter-readings.
remaining_uncertainties: Whether suitable primarily means morally righteous, practically compatible, or both.
Whether the marriage branch of enrichment should color this token or remain a lexical outlier beside a financial sense.
How much of divine provision the ayah depicts as socially mediated rather than direct.
Whether the status-exit arc is one integrated program or several adjacent remedies.
The cloud-gap and split-root readings are exploratory analogies and should not be promoted to direct lexical meanings.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Marriage is communal provisioning that forms a viable household.** **Lexical evidence:** fixed-ayah `ن ك ح` B003 is giving another in marriage and B004 spousal attachment; `ء ي م` B001 is being without a spouse; `ف ق ر` B002 is material need and B008 a back-breaking calamity; `غ ن ي` B001 is self-sufficiency and B006 marriage as protection/sufficiency; `ف ض ل` B003 is bounty and `و س ع` B003 ample means. **Structural cue:** the plural command makes the community arrange marriages; 24:27-31 have defined protected household access, 24:33 joins sexual restraint to economic release, and 24:36-37 present houses sustained by disciplined practice. **Assigned role:** arranged attachment transforms isolated status into household support, while divine bounty answers fear that poverty makes that formation impossible. **Abductive move:** the packet supplies spouselessness, material need, communal action, and promised sufficiency; I infer supported pairing → shared capacity → reduced vulnerability. **Reading change:** the command is social infrastructure for household formation, not merely advice to two private individuals.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 24:33 corrected any purely private reading of marriage-sufficiency: the adjacent manumission funding and anti-coercion commands show that viable households depend on redistributed resources and protected agency. 24:36-37 then show the practices that sustain them.

baseline.text: İçinizden evli olmayanları ve sahip olduğunuz erkek ve kadınlardan iyi olanları evlendirin. Yoksul iseler Allah onları lütfundan zenginleştirir. Allah'ın lütfu geniştir, O bilendir.

findings.text: Topluluğa verilen evlendirme görevi, eşsiz ve yoksul kişileri önceden servet beklemeden desteklenen bir haneye bağlayan toplumsal bir yeterlik düzeni kurar.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: The immediate continuation makes restraint necessary when marriage is unavailable until God grants sufficiency from His favor.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: Its servant-status and divine judgment offer only a remote channel-level resonance with household provision.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: The false claim that God is poor reverses the focus ayah's dependence: people need God, not the reverse.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: Poverty is set against God's promise of forgiveness and favor, directly supporting confidence beyond fear of lack.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: The surah's enacted legal frame supplies broad context but adds no specific account of marriage or provision.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Moses explicitly names his need for whatever good God sends, giving a personal instance of dependence and provision.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: It explicitly contrasts human poverty with God's self-sufficiency and ties that dependence to communal spending.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: Universal divine ownership is a general ground for provision but is less specific than the poverty parallels.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: It directly names people as needy before God and God as self-sufficient, grounding the focus ayah's promise of enrichment.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: A pledge to give charity when granted divine favor shows favor as provision with a social obligation.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: The nearby sexual-law setting gives only broad context for the surah's ordered marital life.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: Its marriage prohibition shows that forming households is regulated by durable kinship boundaries, not mere availability.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: God's favor is given as He wills and the verse closes with the same vast-knowing attributes, though outside marriage and poverty.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: It treats marriage as a socially accountable bond, complementing the focus ayah's command to arrange such bonds.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: Wealth and earnings failing to suffice provide a limited contrast to sufficiency granted by God.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: The identical vast-knowing formula is an attribute echo without a marriage or poverty setting.

inter_ayah_rows.label: strong
inter_ayah_rows.note: After marital separation, God can make each party sufficient from His abundance, a direct marital sufficiency parallel.

inter_ayah_rows.label: medium
inter_ayah_rows.note: It identifies concealed poverty and directs giving toward it, clarifying the communal responsibility around need.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak
inter_ayah_rows.note: Material breadth is denied as the sole measure of fitness, while God grants authority; this is only an indirect capacity parallel.

inter_ayah_rows.label: weak

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: [P2 24:21-34] Marriage Converts Lack into Household Capacity
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Marriage is a transition from unpaired status toward a protected household, mediated by resources, sufficiency, and restraint during delay.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Sufficiency branches explicitly treat marriage itself as enrichment and fortification, while patient delay appears as a controlled temporal operation rather than passive exclusion.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: From Unpaired Status to Contracted Pair
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: A person lacking a spouse is actively brought into a recognized marital bond.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: interruption of spousal pairing `quranic:root_000073:B001/m01`; causing another to enter marriage `quranic:root_001548:B003/m01`; marriage contract `quranic:root_001548:B002/m01`; acquisition of marital affiliation `quranic:root_001548:B004/m01`
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: The unpaired state is not treated as an essence. A communal causative act and a legal bond convert it into affiliation. The operation distributes responsibility beyond the prospective spouses alone.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Poverty Becomes Sufficiency
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Material need is met by an enlarging gift that makes a household viable, with marriage itself functioning as a form of sufficiency.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: material poverty and need `quranic:root_001169:B002/m01`; material independence `quranic:root_001110:B001/m01`; functional sufficiency `quranic:root_001110:B002/m01`; marriage as enrichment and protection `quranic:root_001110:B006/m01`; breadth of means `quranic:root_001647:B003/m01`; unowed divine gift `quranic:root_001163:B003/m01`
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.ayah_anchors: 24:32 `إِن يَكُونُوا فُقَرَاءَ يُغْنِهِمُ اللَّهُ مِن فَضْلِهِ وَاللَّهُ وَاسِعٌ`; 24:33 `حَتَّى يُغْنِيَهُمُ اللَّهُ مِن فَضْلِهِ`
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Enrichment is not reducible to cash accumulation. It includes enough function, widened capacity, and the stabilizing relation created by marriage. The sequence reframes economic lack as a condition that can be transformed rather than a permanent bar.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: [P2 24:21-34] Marriage Converts Lack into Household Capacity
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Marriage is a transition from unpaired status toward a protected household, mediated by resources, sufficiency, and restraint during delay.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Sufficiency branches explicitly treat marriage itself as enrichment and fortification, while patient delay appears as a controlled temporal operation rather than passive exclusion.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Restrained Waiting
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: A person unable to reach marriage holds desire within a guarded boundary until capacity changes.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: restraining oneself from what is improper `quranic:root_001031:B001/m01`; guarded sexual integrity `quranic:root_000331:B002/m01`; gentle pacing and delay `quranic:root_000610:B005/m01`; practical easing of hardship `quranic:root_001647:B005/m01`; useful good sought in the interim `quranic:root_000452:B001/m01`
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.ayah_anchors: 24:32 `وَاللَّهُ وَاسِعٌ`; 24:33 `وَلْيَسْتَعْفِفِ الَّذِينَ لَا يَجِدُونَ نِكَاحًا حَتَّى يُغْنِيَهُمُ اللَّهُ ... إِنْ عَلِمْتُمْ فِيهِمْ خَيْرًا`
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Waiting is an active containment scene with a specified terminus, not indefinite suspension. Restraint protects the sexual boundary while gradual easing and recognized good prepare a changed material state.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: [P2 24:21-34] Dependent Status Can Be Written Toward Release or Forced Toward Exploitation
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Power over dependents takes opposite procedural forms: a written, funded route out of ownership or coercive conversion of another's body into worldly return.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Writing branches assemble, inscribe, bind, and finally emancipate; coercion branches instead override aversion and turn sexual violation into an extractive transaction.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: The Emancipation Contract
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Separated terms are joined into writing, made binding, and directed toward release from owned status.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: joining parts into one construction `quranic:root_001283:B001/m01`; inscribed document `quranic:root_001283:B002/m01`; binding legal determination `quranic:root_001283:B003/m01`; manumission contract for staged payment `quranic:root_001283:B005/m01`; owned human status `quranic:root_001444:B002/m01`; enslaved person opposed to the free `quranic:root_000973:B001/m01`; enslaved youth or servant `quranic:root_001130:B002/m01`
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.ayah_anchors: 24:32 `عِبَادِكُمْ وَإِمَائِكُمْ`; 24:33 `يَبْتَغُونَ الْكِتَابَ مِمَّا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَانُكُمْ فَكَاتِبُوهُمْ`
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: The four writing senses form a procedural sequence: assemble terms, record them, give them binding force, and orient performance toward freedom. The contract is therefore a machine for changing status, not merely a document about it.

error_profile.preserves: Uyku halinin goze baskin gelmesini korur.
Baskin gelme yonunu korur.
error_profile.adds: Rakipli mucadele veya zafer anlamini ekler.
error_profile.collision: Yuklenme ve hedefe dayanma boyutu kaybolabilir.

neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komsu dal daha genel olarak ustun gelme, yenme veya yukselme alanindadir.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Iki dalda da bir seyin digerine ustun gelmesi fikri bulunur.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: B008'de ustunluk bir hedefe dayanma veya onun uzerine agir basma kalibiyla gelir; komsu dal genel galip gelme alaninda daha genistir.

neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komsu dal iki sey arasinda siddetli baski ve ic ice girme anlamindadir.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Iki dal da baski veya yogun temas alanini paylasir.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: B008'de etken bir hedefe baskin gelir; komsuda ise baski ve ic ice girme kendi basina cekirdektir. B008'in yagmur ve uyku kaliplari komsudaki mekanik sikismaya indirgenmez.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Bu dal bir etkenin hedefe yuklenmesi veya baskin gelmesidir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komsu dal gogus veya govdenin yere yapismasi, bastirmasi ya da bununla ezme alanindadir.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Iki dalda da bir yuzeye veya hedefe agirlik verme fikri vardir.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: B008 daha soyut ve kaliplidir: yagmur yere, uyku goze yuklenir. Komsu dal ise bedensel temas ve yere bastirma gibi somut bir baski cekirdegine sahiptir.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Bu dal evlilik disi yuklenme ve baskin gelme kaliplaridir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komsu dal cinsel birlesme anlamindadir.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Iki dal ayni kok ailesi icinde bulunur.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: B008'in kaynak ifadesi yagmur ve uyku kaliplarini verir; bu nedenle evlilik ve cinsel birlesme alanina geri cekilmemelidir. B001'in cekirdegi ise bedensel iliskidir.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Tum aday komsular degerlendirildi; secilenler yuklenme, baskin gelme ve evlilik alanindan kopusu en net aciklayanlardir.

branches.source_phrase_ar: نكح المطر الأرض إذا اعتمد عليها؛ ونكح النعاس عينه إذا غلب عليها (tahdhib)

source_note.TA: Tek kaynakli kanit, yagmurun yere dayanmasi ve uyuklamanin goze galip gelmesi kaliplarini birlikte verir.

root_profile.summary: Bu kok ailesi, cinsel birlesme, evlilik sozlesmesi, baskasini evlendirme, evli olma, evlilik kabul sozu, cinsel davranis yogunlugu, sebep kaynakli evlendirilme ve hedefe yuklenip baskin gelme dallarina ayrilir. Ana evlilik ve iliski alaninin yaninda, yagmur ve uyuklama orneklerinde gorulen aktarilmis bir baskin gelme alani da vardir.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi bu dalın çekirdeğini bozukluğun ve kötülüğün karşıtı olan iyi, düzgün durum olarak kurar; ayrıca bu duruma gelmeyi, bir şeyi bu duruma getirmeyi ve belirli bir yapıda bir canlıya iyi davranmayı da kapsar. Geçici çerçeve bu durum, süreç ve ettirgen işlem ayrımlarını doğru biçimde bir arada tutmaktadır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Kişiler, işler ve şeylerdeki iyi durum ile bu durumu sağlama bu dala girer; kişiler arası uzlaşma, uygunluk ve özel adlar ayrı dallardadır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Dal, yalın biçimlerdeki iyi ve düzgün olma çekirdeğini, düzeltme türevlerini ve yalnızca belirli yapıda görülen iyi davranma kullanımını birbirine karıştırmadan kapsar.

concept_map.definition: Bir kişinin, işin ya da şeyin bozukluğun karşıtı olan iyi ve düzgün durumda bulunması veya bu duruma gelmesi; ayrıca bir şeyi bozukluktan arındırarak iyi duruma getirme işlemidir. Belirli bir yapıda bir canlıya iyi davranma anlamı bu çekirdeğe bağlı özel bir kullanımdır.

facets.statement: Kişi, iş veya şey bozukluğun ve kötülüğün karşıtı olan iyi, düzgün ve yararlı bir durumda bulunur.
Bir şey kendiliğinden iyi ve düzgün duruma gelebilir ya da bir etken bozukluğu gidererek onu bu duruma getirebilir.
İyi duruma getirme, iyi yaratma, var olan bozukluğu giderme veya bir kimsenin iyi olduğuna hükmetme yollarıyla gerçekleşebilir.
Belirli bir yönelme yapısında anlam, bir hayvana iyi davranmaya kadar uzanır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynakların ortak ekseni bozukluğun ve kötülüğün karşıtı olan iyi, düzgün durumdur. Bu eksen kişinin ve işin iyi olmasını, bir şeyi düzeltmeyi, yarar sağlayan şeyi, iyi duruma getirmeyi istemeyi ve özel bir yapıda hayvana iyi davranmayı kapsar; insanın iyi yaratılması, bozukluğunun giderilmesi veya iyi sayılması da düzeltmenin farklı gerçekleşmeleri olarak verilir.

concept_gloss.applicability: Dalın hem durum ve duruma gelme çekirdeğini hem de bozukluğu gidererek iyi duruma getirme işlemini birlikte temsil eder.

error_profile.preserves: İyi ve düzgün durum, bu duruma gelme ve bu durumu sağlama ayrımlarını korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir kişi, iş veya şeyin bozuk olmayan durumunu ya da bu duruma gelmesini anlatan bağlamlarda kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: İyi ve düzgün durumda bulunma ya da bu duruma gelme yönünü korur.
error_profile.loses: Bir şeyi bu duruma getirme işlemini ve özel yapıdaki iyi davranma kullanımını dışarıda bırakır.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir etkenin kişi, iş veya şeydeki bozukluğu gidererek onu iyi duruma getirdiği bağlamlarda kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Bozukluğu giderme ve iyi duruma getirme işlemini korur.
error_profile.loses: Kendiliğinden iyi durumda olmayı ve özel yapıdaki iyi davranma kullanımını karşılamaz.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Yalnızca kaynakta verilen yönelme yapısının bir hayvana yönelik iyi davranışı anlattığı bağlam için uygundur.

error_profile.preserves: Özel yapının iyi davranma anlamını eksiksiz korur.
error_profile.loses: Dalın genel iyi durum ve düzeltme çekirdeğini temsil etmez.

neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: İnsanlar arasındaki soğukluk ve çatışmanın karşılıklı barışmayla giderilmesi komşu dala özgüdür.

neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal nesnelerin, kişilerin ve işlerin niteliğini veya düzeltilmesini anlatır; komşu dal ise yalnızca insanlar arasındaki ilişkinin barışmaya dönüşmesini anlatır.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Bozukluğun karşıtı olan iyi durum ve bu durumu sağlama odak dala özgüdür.
